chunks: And a group informed me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh and others, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, from Ali ibn Qays, from some of the officials of al-Sawad, who said:

I saw Nasim recently in Sarman Ra'ya, and he had broken the door of the house. A person came out to him holding a tabrazin (axe), and asked: 'What are you doing in my house?' Nasim said: 'Ja'far claimed that your father has passed away and has no issue. If this is your house, then it has reverted to you,' so he left the house. Ali ibn Qays said: 'A servant from the house's staff came to us, and I asked him about this news. He said: 'Who told you about this?' I said: 'Some official of al-Sawad told me.' He said to me: 'Nothing hardly escapes the people's notice.'

key_terms.ابْنُ قَيْسٍ: Ibn Qays, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.السَّوَاد: Al-Sawad, the region of southern Iraq (specifically around Kufa/Basra)
key_terms.سَرْمَنْ رَأَى: Sarmen Ra'ya, a city in Iraq where the Imam resided during the Minor Occultation
key_terms.طَبْرَزِين: Tabrazin, a type of axe or hatchet

ai.seo_question: What happened when Nasim entered the house of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) in Sarman Ra'ya?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the concept of *al-Ghayb al-Saghir* (Minor Occultation) by demonstrating that while the Imam was concealed from the general public to avoid persecution, his presence was known to specific witnesses like Nasim. The incident underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s life was not a total secret but rather a guarded reality, where local officials and servants could verify his existence, thereby validating the continuity of the Imamate during the period of concealment.
